title: Venice Horizons Best Director Winner Anuparna Roy’s ‘Lovers in the Blue Night’ Boarded by Parallax (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Parallax has acquired international sales rights to Anuparna Roy’s “Lovers in the Blue Night,” which will have its world premiere in the Horizons co
body:
Parallax has acquired international sales rights to Anuparna Roy’s “Lovers in the Blue Night,” which will have its world premiere in the Horizons competition at the Venice Film Festival.

	The film brings Roy back to the Lido one year after she became the first Indian filmmaker to win the Horizons best director prize, an honor she took for her debut feature, “Songs of Forgotten Trees.”


	Set amid Mumbai’s restless nightlife, “Lovers in the Blue Night” centers on four migrants whose lives intertwine: a husband hiding his sexuality, his lonely wife who works in a bar, a petty criminal and a man who trades in sex work. Their paths converge through unlikely romance, hidden longing and a shared fight to survive and belong.
	

	“We were deeply impressed by the film’s delicate and nuanced portrayal of human emotions,” said Parallax’s Liuying Cao. “Rather than relying on dramatic gestures, it finds remarkable strength in subtle moments, which stayed with us long after the screening. We are also very excited by Anuparna Roy’s distinct directorial voice. We sincerely hope to accompany her and her future works on their international journey, beginning with ‘Lovers in the Blue Night.'”


	The production is backed by Vikas Kumar of Khan & Kumar Media, Sharib Khan of Ammi Media, Bibhanshu Rai and Romil Modi, who previously worked together on Roy’s “Songs of Forgotten Trees.” The team has since grown with the addition of U.S.-based Rhet Topham as producer, U.S.-based Beesham Sreecharan as executive producer and London-based Amar Singh as associate producer, joining executive producer Neeraj Churi.
	

	The cast includes Neelima Sharma, Pritam Pilania, Bhushan Shimpi, Jatin Sarin, Kajal Keshav, Swetha Mishra and Vinod Suryavanshi. Roy also wrote the story. Debjit Samanta served as cinematographer, Ketul Thakkar edited the film and Nishant Ramtake composed the original score.

title: Dolly Parton Has One Last Song Buried in a Time Capsule: ‘My Place In History’
description: Country queen and national treasure Dolly Parton may have physically left the world on Tuesday, but her indelible mark on the world and the industry
body:
Country queen and national treasure Dolly Parton may have physically left the world on Tuesday, but her indelible mark on the world and the industry will never be forgotten. And luckily, she’s not done yet. Parton has several posthumous projects to look forward to, one of which is a secret song. 

	Back in 2015, Parton and her team buried a chestnut box filled with physical copies of a brand new song in two formats, cassette and CD, along with their corresponding players, under her Dollywood DreamMore Resort and Spa. The time capsule is meant to remain sealed off until after the park celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2045, in time for Parton’s 100th birthday. 
	

	A placard within the box reads, “The chestnut ‘Dream Box’ is a repository of Dolly’s wishes and memories for the future. It will not be opened until Dolly’s birthday on January 19, 2046. The Dream Box itself is tribute to her original mentor and uncle, Bill Owens, who has worked tirelessly to preserve the American Chestnut tree. As a final tribute, Dolly placed a song which she has written to be released as her last. Entitled ‘My Place In History,’ only Dolly will know its melody and content until 2046.” 

	Parton explained to Kelly Clarkson on the “The Kelly Clarkson Show” in 2022 that the vault track does in fact exist. She even acknowledged that she might not be around for the reveal of the unreleased track. 

	“They weren’t expecting me to be there at all,” Parton said. “I’m just saying, I might be there. Who knows? But the point is, there is a song – I figure it’ll probably disintegrate, probably nobody ever hears it. That’s what bothers me, to think that it’s gonna be a song that nobody’s ever gonna hear if it rots in there before they open it.”
	

	While it’s been over 11 years since its burial, Parton insisted it was a song worth unearthing – eventually. 

	“It’s a really good song,” she added. “But yes, I have a song that’s buried that nobody’s gonna hear – I don’t know whose damn idea that was.”

	Parton died after a “brief battle” with cancer at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville, her reps said Tuesday. 

	“Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched. Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand,” the statement from her reps to People magazine read.

	Several other endeavors remain in place after her death. Parton was working on a new Nashville museum and hotel, deals to endorse Purina dog treats and launch her Cup of Ambition coffee brand. The musical based on her life, “Dolly, A True Original Musical,” will open on Broadway on Jan. 19, 2027, which would have been her 81st birthday.

schema.headline: Dolly Parton Has One Last Song Buried in a Time Capsule: ‘My Place In History’

title: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Cast and Crew Held a ‘Funeral Screening’ After the Movie Was Shelved: ‘Was Emotional in So Many Ways’
description:
What do you do when you think your movie will never see the light of day? Have a “funeral screening,” of course.

	That’s exactly what the team behi
body:
What do you do when you think your movie will never see the light of day? Have a “funeral screening,” of course.

	That’s exactly what the team behind “Coyote vs. Acme” did when they feared the live-action-animation hybrid comedy was locked in the Warner Bros. vault for good. Luckily, after WB. shelved the project, Ketchup Entertainment scooped up the title from the studio in March 2025 and slated it for theatrical release. Audiences will finally get to see the “Looney Tunes” movie on Aug. 28.
	

	When asked what it was like walking into the “funeral screening,” star Lana Condor told Variety at the film’s L.A. premiere on Wednesday, “It’s so horrible. It’s like, really easy to blame yourself. You almost feel like, ‘Was I the problem?’ You’re devastated for the hundreds of people who have worked on this far longer than I have. It feels like a funeral.”


	Director Dave Green said there were “many, many times” he thought “Coyote vs. Acme” would never come out. Despite his disappointment, he described the mood at the “funeral screening” as “celebratory.”

	“You can have a New Orleans funeral, [with] a jazz band walking up the street, just having a celebration,” Green joked. “That screening for us was emotional in so many ways. It was a bit of a party because we were able to share the movie with friends and other filmmakers who had never seen the movie. And I got to share it with Will [Forte] and Lana, who never got to see the final movie. So that moment was so charged and electric, and the room played so hot.”
	

	“Coyote vs. Acme” sees “Looney Tunes” villain Wile E. Coyote take the Acme Corporation to court after being injured countless times from using its gadgets (think rocket-powered skates and anvils). Condor and Will Forte star. Other cast members include John Cena, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán, P.J. Byrne and John Early.

title: COL Group, Virtue Asia and V47 Entertainment Launch Inside Microdramas, Vertical Entertainment Upfront
description: COL Group, Virtue Asia and V47 Entertainment have unveiled Inside Microdramas, billed as the first upfront event built around microdramas and the br
body:
COL Group, Virtue Asia and V47 Entertainment have unveiled Inside Microdramas, billed as the first upfront event built around microdramas and the broader vertical entertainment business. 

	The event will take place in Singapore on Oct. 27.

	The initiative is expected to draw senior executives from entertainment, advertising, tech, platforms and consumer brands.


	Inside Microdramas draws a distinction between microdrama, defined as a specific short-form, serialized storytelling format, and vertical entertainment, a broader term spanning scripted series, reality and factual programming, creator-driven content, interactive narratives, commerce tie-ins and branded IP, all shaped for how audiences watch on phones.
	

	“Microdramas are not the entire story. They are the first signal of a much bigger shift in how entertainment is created, distributed, funded and consumed,” said Timothy Oh, general manager, international, at COL Group. “Inside Microdramas is designed to move the conversation beyond the format itself and explore the wider vertical entertainment economy emerging around it. It will also give brands the opportunity to participate much earlier, not simply as advertisers, but as partners in building the next generation of entertainment IP.”

	“The next evolution of branded entertainment will not come from placing brands into stories after they have already been developed. It will come from bringing brands, creators and producers together at the very beginning,” said David Webster, chair of V47 Entertainment. “This upfront creates a marketplace for that collaboration, where original ideas can find the right partners, funding and distribution to become entertainment audiences genuinely choose to watch.”
	

	Organized around the theme Inside the Business, Culture and Future of Entertainment’s Fastest-Growing Format, the program mixes panel discussions, brand viewpoints, cross-sector debate, previews of upcoming projects and dedicated one-on-one partnership meetings.

	COL Group will open with a session titled The New Rules of Attention, examining why microdramas are pushing studios, platforms and creators toward new thinking on how stories get made, distributed and watched as mobile becomes the primary screen. Virtue Asia will present Why Brands Need Entertainment, Not More Content, exploring how brands can move from advertising around culture to actively creating the stories and characters audiences choose to follow. V47 Entertainment will host a cross-industry panel, Are Brands Becoming the New Studios?, bringing together brands, platforms, production and entertainment representatives to examine new funding and distribution economics.

	The event’s centerpiece, First Look: The 2027 Slate, will give a first look at creator-led intellectual property and original vertical entertainment concepts from COL Group and V47 Entertainment. Some 10 projects will be shown to prospective brand partners for possible development and production, letting companies get involved before projects are fully financed or produced. Invited guests will then join dedicated Greenlight Sessions, sitting down with the project teams to talk through commissions, financing, distribution and co-development.

	More details on where the event will be held, who will speak and what makes the slate are due out in the coming weeks.

	COL Group builds digital entertainment and technology products, including the FlareFlow vertical drama app. Virtue Asia is a strategic and creative agency whose clients include Disney, Google, Spotify, Toyota, Diageo and Shiseido. V47 Entertainment was formed by Virtue Asia and Goldfinch International, the international growth arm of the U.K.’s Goldfinch Group, which has backed more than 200 film and TV projects and put $300 million into production.

schema.headline: COL Group, Virtue Asia and V47 Entertainment Launch Inside Microdramas, Vertical Entertainment Upfront

title: Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton, Completely Revamps Setlist at Madison Square Garden Opening Night: Concert Review
description: Apart from the special show he performed with an orchestra in London, Harry Styles has played basically the same set since his “Together, Together”
body:
Apart from the special show he performed with an orchestra in London, Harry Styles has played basically the same set since his “Together, Together” tour opened in Amsterdam 33 shows and nearly three months ago. But for the opening night of his unprecedented 30-show stand at New York’s Madison Square Garden on Wednesday, he completely overhauled the set, drastically re-ordering the songs, rearranging several older ones, and performing one song publicly for the first time.
	

	He also took a moment to pay brief but loving tribute to Dolly Parton, whose death was announced on Tuesday, pausing for a moment late in the show to say, “I just wanna give a proper thank you to all the musicians who have inspired me over the years — Dolly, we love you. Thank you so much.” Then her recording of “I Will Always Love You” — of course, her best-known song and one of the biggest hits in history when covered by Whitney Houston — played over the P.A. for a minute before he carried on the show.



	It was clear from the show’s opening notes that this one would be different: Styles took the stage to “Dance No More,” replacing the previous opener “Are You Listening Yet?,” and then launched into “Carolina,” a deep from his solo debut, which he hadn’t performed live since that first solo tour. From there, songs that were previously played late in the set were performed early (and vice versa), and mid-set, “The Waiting Game” from his latest album, “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.,” got its live debut.
	


	Early in the show, Styles thanked opening act Jamie XX and then took a moment to acknowledge a full-circle moment on this opening night. “I was told a story when I got here today,” he said. “I had the great privilege of playing this building for the first time when I was 18 years old,” he said, referencing One Direction’s debut at the venue in 2012. “There’s a gentleman who’s working here who hwas working here then, who shared with me that when I got out of the car that day, I kissed the floor and said, ‘I’ve made it to Madison Square Garden!’” The crowd erupted in cheers.

Harry Styles tells a story about how he kissed the floor right before his first-ever performance at Madison Square Garden. He was 18 years old.Tonight, the artist is kicking off Night 1 of his sold-out 30-show “Together, Together” residency at the iconic New York venue. pic.twitter.com/eT9ItgBETb— Variety (@Variety) August 27, 2026


	Thus far, the “Together, Together” tour has played multiple shows in Amsterdam, London, São Paulo and Mexico City. Following the New York run, which concludes with Styles’ annual dress-up “Harryween” concert on October 31, the tour heads to Melbourne and Sydney in December. Special guests across select dates include Robyn, Shania Twain, Jamie xx, Jorja Smith, Fousheé, Fcukers and Skye Newman.

	Additional reporting by Jem Aswad.

	Encore:(Dolly Parton tribute)Sign of the TimesAperture

title: Leah Remini Joins ‘The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills’ Season 16
description: Season 16 of “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” has a new marquee star: The Bravo show has landed actor/anti-Scientology activist Leah Remini as
body:
Season 16 of “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” has a new marquee star: The Bravo show has landed actor/anti-Scientology activist Leah Remini as a full-time cast member.

	Remini won’t be the only new cast member on “RHOBH.” Tracy Tutor, the real estate agent and former “Million Dollar Listing Los Angeles” star announced on Instagram on Aug. 19 that she’s also joining the cast. Remini and Tutor will co-star with returning full-time cast members Kyle Richards, Erika “Jayne” Girardi, Dorit Kemsley, Bozoma Saint John, Rachel Zoe and Sutton Stracke. Kathy Hilton and Jennifer Tilly will also be back as “friends” of the cast. Amanda Frances — the manifesting guru added to the cast for its 15th season — was not asked back, despite Rihanna’s DM to Frances saying, “We need more of you!” Frances herself announced her own departure on Instagram on Aug. 5.
	

	Season 16 has already begun filming, with several of the cast (though not Remini and Tutor) attending Saint John’s wedding to Keely Watson in Ghana on Aug. 21. Kemsley, Richards, Tilly and Stracke were among the guests. Remini will begin filming in Los Angeles later this week.


	“The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” is the most-watched edition of the “Real Housewives” franchise, which turned 20 this year. Within segments of the Bravosphere, it’s also the most complained about, with quibbling fans constantly calling for a major cast overhaul, year after year. As executive producer Andy Cohen put it sarcastically in an interview with Variety in June, “They hate it so much, it’s the No. 1 ‘Housewives.'” Now, with eight full-time cast members and two veteran (and popular) friends, perhaps this full deck of Housewives will tamp down the griping. It will certainly put an end to the rampant (and incorrect) speculation about the Season 16 cast, which has included an anonymous tip to DeuxMoi claiming that Kyle had filmed a farewell scene during production on “Real Housewives Ultimate Girls Trip Roaring 20th” and a blind item sent to Bravo and Cocktails that said Dorit was being put on pause. (Executive producer Alex Baskin debunked the Kemsley report, which had spread far and wide.) There was also speculation that Crystal Kung Minkoff, who was on Seasons 11-13, might rejoin the cast, especially after she was featured on “Ultimate Girls Trip.”
	

	Remini and Tutor’s new associates are a divided group — Season 15 concluded in May after a fiery three-part reunion, during which the tension between Richards and Kemsley, who were once close friends, boiled over. Kemsley’s divorce from Paul “PK” Kemsley has continued to make headlines over the summer, with both of them accusing the other of financial mayhem, with their school-age children stuck in the middle.

	Remini, 56, became a household name during the nine-season-long run of “King of Queens” on CBS. In 2015, she released the memoir “Troublemaker: Surviving Hollywood and Scientology,” in which she recounted her rise in Hollywood as well as her indoctrination into Scientology beginning at age 9. (“Where is Shelly?” Remini has asked since 2006, wondering about the whereabouts of Shelly Miscavige, the never-seen wife of Scientology leader David Miscavige). Remini’s high-profile exit from the organization caused her to become an anti-cult crusader, and she and fellow ex-Scientologist Mike Rinder hosted “Leah Remini: Scientology and the Aftermath” on A&E, winning two primetime Emmys for the series along the way.

	As for Tutor, 51, she’s no stranger to Bravo. As a successful real estate agent, Tutor starred on the network’s long-running show “Million Dollar Listing Los Angeles” from Seasons 10 through 15, before it was put on pause last year. Tutor has long seemed to fans like an obvious choice to join “RHOBH,” and on her Instagram post, Cohen wrote, “This has been a long time coming!”

schema.headline: Leah Remini Joins ‘The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills’ Season 16

title: Manoj Bajpayee’s ‘Last Man in Tower’ Sets September Indian Release From Rana Daggubati’s Spirit Media, Unveils Teaser (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Last Man in Tower,” the Aravind Adiga adaptation starring Manoj Bajpayee, is headed to Indian theaters this September and has unveiled its first te
body:
“Last Man in Tower,” the Aravind Adiga adaptation starring Manoj Bajpayee, is headed to Indian theaters this September and has unveiled its first teaser. 

	The film, directed by Ben Rekhi and produced by Rana Daggubati‘s Spirit Media, will mark the first time Bajpayee and co-star Boman Irani have shared the screen.

	Adapted from Adiga’s novel of the same name – the author also wrote Booker-winning “The White Tiger” – the screenplay was written by Sooni Taraporevala, with Hindi-language dialogue by Juhi Chaturvedi. Divya Dutta completes the principal trio, with Sukant Goel also in the cast.
	

	The story follows Masterji, a retired schoolteacher whose refusal to go along with those around him places him in direct conflict with his own community. His act of quiet resistance ripples outward, throwing into relief the choices and compromises of neighbors – including Mrs. Puri – as an offer of change tests what each of them is willing to hold on to.


	Rekhi said: “It’s been a deeply fulfilling experience bringing ‘Last Man in Tower’ to life with an incredible team top to bottom, from Rana Daggubati producing, to Sooni Taraporevala scripting, all based on Aravind Adiga’s incredible book. The most rewarding part has been witnessing the power of Manoj and Boman – two giants of cinema – working together for the first time in this film. Divya brings an incredible depth and emotional strength to the ensemble, and the combination of these three actors makes the world of the film particularly special. ‘Last Man in Tower’ is an urgent story about holding onto community and family through turbulent times… a story that has only become more relevant with time.”
	

	The release will also be a milestone for Spirit Media, the Hyderabad-based company “Baahubali” star Daggubati founded in 2005: it is the outfit’s first Hindi feature production.

	Daggubati said: “‘Last Man in Tower’ is a deeply human story. What drew us to it was how naturally it finds something universal in the lives of a very specific group of people. There is something very compelling about the way it explores the choices we make and the things we hold on to. The entire ensemble of cast led by Manoj, Divya, and Boman bring an incredible depth to their characters. ‘Last Man in Tower’ also marks an important milestone for Spirit Media as our first Hindi feature production, and our continued effort towards creating space for fresh new stories and voices for the big-screen audience.”

	Rekhi is a Los Angeles-based director whose credits include the SXSW Audience Award-winning “Waterborne” and “Watch List,” which earned 11 nominations at the Filipino Oscars and won two. His documentary short “The Breakthrough Group” was qualified for the 2026 Academy Awards in the best documentary short subject category. “Last Man in Tower” is his sixth feature.

	Music is by Govind Vasantha; cinematography by Rangarajan Ramabadran. Additional producers are Guneet Dogra and Pratiksha Rao.

	“Last Man in Tower” opens in Indian theaters on Sept. 11.

title: ‘The Sandlot’ Cast Reunites for ‘Dugout Dads’ Comedy Series, Chris Paul Signs on to Executive Produce
description:
“Dugout Dads,” the nine-episode series streaming on YouTube, is seeking a bigger playing field.

	The short-form series, created by Patrick Renna an
body:
“Dugout Dads,” the nine-episode series streaming on YouTube, is seeking a bigger playing field.

	The short-form series, created by Patrick Renna and Kyle Howard’s Hambino Media, reunites the cast of 1993 hit “The Sandlot” for a new coming-of-age sports story. The comedy, which dropped on YouTube on Wednesday, stars Renna, Tom Guiry, Chauncey Leopardi, Marty York, Brandon Quintin Adams, Victor DiMattia, Shane Obedzinski, Grant Gelt, Will Horneff and Michael Pena. Danielle Fishel stars as Renna’s character’s wife.
	

	The series tells the story of an idealistic dad (Renna) who volunteers to coach his kids’ Little League team and learns that the adults involved — ie., coaches, parents, and maybe himself — are more unruly than the kids. The storyline was inspired by Renna’s own experience meeting other dads at his own kids’ games.


	On Wednesday, Oh Dip!!! Entertainment came on as executive producers, led by NBA all-star Chris Paul and his brother, CJ Paul. The duo formed the company with top documentary studio Words + Pictures to launch Ohh Dip!!! Entertainment last year, to produce content about sports and entertainment.

	“It looks like you guys need a ninth,” Paul said in an Instagram video on a FaceTime with Renna. “I loved everything that I saw. My production company, we want to get involved and try to take this thing to the next level.” 



	

	



	“This experience has been one I will never forget,” Renna wrote on Instagram on Wednesday as the series was released. “Being back on a field filming a show with my brothers was something I wasn’t sure would happen again. We so appreciate each and every one of you that’s been with us for the last 30+ years! This is a passion project we’ve wanted to do for years and it wouldn’t have been possible without you! Hope you enjoy it as much as we enjoyed making it.”
	

	The “Dugout Dads” team is hopeful that the first short-form season will lead to a full-length season, viewing this batch of episodes as their pre-season.

	“Dugout Dads” is written by Sebastian Jones and Dan Kopelman and is directed by Victor Nelli Jr. Victoria Fradkin produces. All episodes are streaming on YouTube now.

schema.headline: ‘The Sandlot’ Cast Reunites for ‘Dugout Dads’ Comedy Series, Chris Paul Signs on to Executive Produce

title: Beyoncé Announces $1 Million Donation for Earthquake Relief Efforts in Colombia
description: Beyoncé has announced that she will make a personal donation of $1 million to support relief efforts in Colombia following the country’s recent eart
body:
Beyoncé has announced that she will make a personal donation of $1 million to support relief efforts in Colombia following the country’s recent earthquake.

	According to a release from Parkwood Entertainment on Tuesday, the donation will provide food and housing supplies to areas most affected by the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck Chocó, Colombia, on August 10. The release encourages those who can help to visit websites for Food For the Poor and World Central Kitchen.
	

	At least 312 people were killed in the earthquake earlier this month, according to AP, and 29,000 homes were destroyed. According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, 69,000 people in Chocó — or about 10 percent of its population — were affected or displaced by the earthquake.


	Beyoncé joins a growing list of musicians who are raising and donating money for earthquake relief in recent weeks. Shakira, a Colombian native, met with Chocó’s governor and mayor to hear about the impact of the earthquake and committed $1.25 million to help rebuild affected schools. That sum included $500,000 from the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, a $500,000 match from the Fund from Live Nation, and $250,000 from CAF.

	“These past few days, I’ve watched my country suffer, but I’ve also watched people come together with the resilience and solidarity that has always defined us,” said Shakira in a statement. “Schools are more than buildings. They give children the stability and routine they need most after a disaster. That’s why we’re making an initial $1.25 million commitment to help rebuild schools and get children back into their classrooms. Chocó is not alone. Colombia is not alone. And we will keep going.”
	

	Additionally, Karol G donated $1.2 million to earthquake victims through her foundation, while the Colombian band Morat announced that they will donate a portion of ticket sales from their Bogotá residency.

schema.headline: Beyoncé Announces $1 Million Donation for Earthquake Relief Efforts in Colombia

title: ‘Who Has Time to Watch All This Crap?’: Inside 10 Anonymous Emmy Ballots as Voting Officially Closes
description:
Emmy voting is now closed, and not a moment too soon.

	Every year, more than 27,000 members of the Television Academy — actors and editors, showrun
body:
Emmy voting is now closed, and not a moment too soon.

	Every year, more than 27,000 members of the Television Academy — actors and editors, showrunners and composers, the people who actually make television — sit down with their ballots and decide who walks away with an Emmy. And every year, almost none of them will tell us, on the record, what they really think.

	So, like we do with Oscar voters, we reached out to a few of them ourselves.
	

	In the final days of voting for the 78th Emmy Awards, Variety spoke with dozens of Academy members across the organization’s 31 professional peer groups — the specialty divisions that sort the membership by craft, from performers to picture editors — and promised each of them anonymity in exchange for total candor. What we saw was a very small snapshot of where the race could go when awards are handed out across the first two weekends in September.


	Every voter was also asked the same four questions off the ballot — their biggest snub, the most overspent FYC campaign, the network or streamer having the best season and the one win that would actually move the business. Their answers close each entry. 

	In the categories deemed “area awards” — hosted nonfiction and variety series — voters have the opportunity to select multiple nominees by answering a simple question: Does this show deserve an Emmy? Yes or No. Interestingly, not one voter Variety spoke with checked “Yes” for every nominee, and only four of those surveyed selected more than one. That strongly suggests voters aren’t viewing these categories as an opportunity to spread the wealth, but rather as a traditional “may the best show win” competition.
	

	Ballots have been edited for length and, where necessary, to protect identities.

	The opinions are their own. They’re contradictory, occasionally indefensible and, at least for the purposes of this article, the only ones that matter.

	Notably, and vitally important to point out, 10 ballots are not an official presidential poll. They are barely even a focus group. But what you get is a window into a small, unscientific and anecdotal sample of a voting body of more than 20,000 industry professionals. Nobody should mistake this for a forecast, and the voters themselves would be the first to tell you as well (except for one, anyway).

	What these conversations reveal, year after year, is how little of the field any one voter has actually seen. Most watch a fraction of what they’re voting on, then default to what they feel they’re supposed to pick — the title everyone’s talking about. It’s a very human way to fill out a ballot, and it makes Emmy voters a notably more out-of-the-loop bunch than the Oscar crowd I sample every season, who at least tend to show they’ve done their homework.

	If you fold in what these 10 told us — and what they suspect their colleagues are quietly doing — the picture that emerges looks an awful lot like the one the pundits have been sketching all along.

	“The Pitt” looks poised to take drama in a runaway. Comedy is most definitely “Widow’s Bay” against “Hacks,” though the freshman holds a considerable edge over the departing champ. And in limited series, the expected “Beef” vs. “DTF St. Louis” duel is real — but I was struck by how much affection kept surfacing for “The Beast in Me.” Call it, at the very least, a spoiler worth watching.

	The first two nights celebrating the artisans and the Governors Gala will take place on Sept. 5-6. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards air Sept. 14 on NBC.

	Final Emmy predictions will be revealed before the first ceremony date.



	

					Noah Wyle in “The Pitt”
									HBO Max
	


	
		VOTER 1 — The Suit Who Didn’t Watch but Voted Anyway	

	Peer group: Television Executives

	“Who has time to watch all this crap?”

	Official votes submitted:


Drama Series: “The Pitt”
Comedy Series: “Widow’s Bay”
Limited or Anthology Series: “All Her Fault”
Movie: “Tom Clancy’s Jack Ryan: Ghost War”
Game Show: “Jeopardy!”
Hosted or Nonfiction Series: “The Daily Show Presents: Jordan Klepper Fingers the Pulse: Give the Man a Prize” (Y); “Finding Your Roots with Henry Louis Gates Jr.” (No); “My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” (No); “The Reluctant Traveler with Eugene Levy” (No); “Tucci in Italy” (No)
Reality Competition Program: “Survivor”
Short Form Comedy, Drama or Variety Series: “Colbert Before Air”
Short Form Nonfiction or Reality Series: “Inside the Pitt”

title: Panda Express Employee Stands Over Food While Cleaning Fryer
description:
Panda Express Worker Cleaning
                          Chemical Fried Rice, Anyone?!?
body:
Panda Express Worker Cleaning
                          Chemical Fried Rice, Anyone?!?
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 26, 2026
                            5:33 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Panda Express customer says he was stunned when he saw an employee standing on top of a fryer station and spraying cleaning chemicals as food was being prepared below ... and it’s all on video.
      
    
      
      A fast-food customer was left stunned when he recently walked into a Panda Express restaurant in Wisconsin and saw an employee stepping around food as he was cleaning a frying station.The employee then started spraying the chemical and wiping while standing over the food. pic.twitter.com/z0sgr6dz6O
              @ABC7
  
    
            The footage, recorded in early July at a Milwaukee location, shows a worker stepping between fry baskets while cleaning the hood area above them. At one point, a female employee reaches through his legs to place a bowl of food into one of the baskets.
      
    
            The customer who recorded it says he watched the employee jump onto the fryer shortly after food had been put in ... then begin spraying chemicals and wiping while standing right over it.
      

                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Panda Express says it acted immediately once the video came to its attention. "The behavior shown does not meet our food safety or workplace safety standards," a spokesperson said. "We took corrective action, conducted retraining, and reinforced safety procedures with the restaurant team and in the region."
      
    
            The company adds the safety of its guests and employees remains its top priority.
      
    
            No word yet on if the customer's fortune cookie predicted this.

title: CoolKicks LA Owner Claims He Wasn't Charged In Stolen Sneaker Bust
description:
CoolKicks LA Owner
                          I'm Clearing My Name ... In Stolen Sneaker Raid!!!
body:
CoolKicks LA Owner
                          I'm Clearing My Name ... In Stolen Sneaker Raid!!!
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            CoolKicks LA owner Adeel Shams is taking to the internet to clear his name in the stolen sneaker raid at his store last October.
      
    
            Adeel posted a lengthy video Wednesday, explaining no criminal charges were filed against him or CoolKicks in the incident.
      
    
            While Adeel and other employees were detained during the bust, he was later released with no charges and he was never arrested ... nor was he named in the indictment.
      

                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            It turns out 6 Nike employees had been indicted for their involvement in the alleged theft ring ... and CoolKicks co-founder Bereket Abraham was also named.
      
    
            CoolKicks tells TMZ ... Bereket is innocent until proven guilty, but the company has parted ways with him following the indictment.
      
    
            Adeel says he hopes the charges against his former collaborator aren't true and that he has the opportunity to clear his name.

            The NFL is checking to see if Jed York's prostitution arrest has violated their conduct policy.
      
    
            Commissioner Roger Goodell said at the owners' meeting in Atlanta Wednesday that the League is looking into it.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He said ... "It's being reviewed under the personal conduct policy. We'll do that and when there's something to be reported we'll talk."
      

        
                    
                  
      
    
            As you know, body cam footage showed the San Francisco 49ers owner getting busted in Ohio ... still wearing his wedding ring, even though he and his wife split months ago.
      
    
            Jed was arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution ... and later pleaded no contest to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools (a cell phone).
